title_question: How do teams of AI agents work together?
one_liner: Instead of asking one AI model to do everything, a multi-agent system divides big jobs among specialized AI helpers that check each other's work.

steps.title: Complex tasks overwhelm a single prompt
steps.text: When a single language model tries to research sources, outline strategy, draft paragraphs, and format code all at once, errors and oversights accumulate quickly.

stage_state.description: Single model icon struggling under multiple competing task instructions.

steps.title: Specialized roles are assigned
steps.text: The system creates distinct virtual agents with focused system instructions: a Researcher gathers facts, a Writer drafts text, and a Critic inspects for quality.

stage_state.description: Three focused agent avatars with specific tool badges (Search, Drafting, Review).

steps.title: A supervisor orchestrates handoffs
steps.text: A coordinator agent manages conversation state, routes intermediate results between roles, and halts execution when the objective is met.

stage_state.description: Central router directing message traffic between specialized agent nodes.

steps.title: Collaborative critique catches mistakes
steps.text: Before presenting the result, the critic agent compares the draft against your initial guidelines and sends back targeted suggestions for revision.

stage_state.description: Feedback loop returning draft for revision before final delivery checkmark.

analogy.text: Think of it like a newsroom. Rather than asking a single person to report from the field, write the article, fact-check claims, and format the printed paper alone, the newsroom divides the work: a reporter uncovers facts, an editor verifies sources, and a copywriter polishes the phrasing.
analogy.breaks: Human journalists possess real-world judgment and common sense. AI agents can get trapped in repetitive critique loops or reinforce each other's misunderstandings if the supervisor router lacks strict iteration limits.

myth.claim: Deploying more AI agents in a swarm will solve every complex problem.
myth.reality: Adding too many agents introduces communication latency, token expense, and coordination confusion. A tight loop of two specialized roles (creator and reviewer) frequently outperforms large, noisy swarms.

seen_in: Autonomous research tools like Perplexity Deep Research or Devin
Customer support pipelines where one bot triages and another resolves
Software development agents collaborating across coding, test generation, and code review

persona_examples.student: Using a researcher agent to extract study points from lecture slides while a quiz agent formats flashcards from those exact excerpts.
persona_examples.teacher: Having a creator agent draft lesson activities while a standards agent verifies that every problem aligns with grade-level curriculum objectives.
persona_examples.entrepreneur: Automating customer onboarding where an intake agent verifies account details, a drafter prepares credentials, and an auditor logs records in your CRM.
persona_examples.engineer_office: Orchestrating an implementation agent, a unit-test generation agent, and a security checker that inspect code pull requests before human review.

quiz.question: What is the primary advantage of a multi-agent architecture over one monolithic prompt?
options: It eliminates the need for computer hardware
It divides complex workflows into specialized roles with independent evaluation and critique
It translates all responses into audio automatically
It prevents models from using computer memory
quiz.explanation: Specialized roles allow individual agents to focus on specific tasks (like research or critique) rather than getting confused trying to accomplish everything in a single prompt.

quiz.question: What critical role does the supervisor agent (or orchestrator) perform?
options: Coordinates message passing, decides which agent acts next, and enforces stopping conditions
quiz.explanation: The supervisor orchestrates the state machine, routes work between agents, and halts execution when tasks complete or hit loop limits.

quiz.question: What can occur if a multi-agent system lacks proper stopping limits or supervision?
options: The computer display will switch off
Agents can enter infinite critique loops, endlessly rewriting without converging while consuming tokens and time
The computer hard drive deletes itself
quiz.explanation: Without maximum iteration counts and clear completion criteria, agents can bounce feedback back and forth indefinitely.

explain_back.prompt: Complete this sentence to prove you understand:
explain_back.template: A multi-agent architecture divides complex tasks among specialized AI roles that coordinate and review each other's work, which helps catch mistakes that a single prompt might miss.

bullets: Topologies: Sequential pipelines, Hierarchical supervisor routing (hub-and-spoke), and Networked graph-based state machines (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI).
State management: Shared global state versus localized message history prevents context window saturation across multi-turn interactions.
Termination criteria: Enforcing maximum iteration bounds (e.g. k <= 4) and token budgets avoids runaway recursive loops.
Human-in-the-loop checkpoints: Suspending execution state allows human operators to inspect and approve sensitive external actions before dispatch.
